sections.heading: Setting up with respect to y, and total area

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by $x = y^2$ and $x = 2y$ by integrating with respect to $y$.
Find the total area between $f(x) = \sin x$ and the $x$-axis on $[0, 2\pi]$ (note the curve is below the axis on part of this interval).
questions.answer: By symmetry, $\int_0^\pi \sin x\,dx = 2$ and $\left|\int_\pi^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx\right| = 2$. Total area $= 2 + 2 = 4$.

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by $y=x^2-4$ and $y=4-x^2$.
questions.answer: Intersections: $x^2-4=4-x^2$, so $2x^2=8$, $x=\pm2$. Upper curve is $y=4-x^2$: Area $=\int_{-2}^{2}\left[(4-x^2)-(x^2-4)\right]dx = \int_{-2}^2(8-2x^2)\,dx = \left[8x-\frac{2x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^2 = \frac{64}{3}$.

questions.q: Find the area between $y=x^3$ and $y=x$ on $[0,1]$ (note that $y=x$ is above $y=x^3$ on this interval).
Find the area between $y=x^3$ and $y=x$ on $[-1,1]$ (note the curves cross at $x=0$, so the identity of the upper curve switches).
questions.answer: On $[-1,0]$, $x^3\geq x$; on $[0,1]$, $x\geq x^3$. Area $=\int_{-1}^0(x^3-x)\,dx+\int_0^1(x-x^3)\,dx$. By symmetry both integrals equal $\frac{1}{4}$ (using the earlier result), so total area $=\frac{1}{2}$.

sections.heading: Visualizing a region bounded by two curves

questions.q: The graphs of $f(x)=x^2-4$ and $g(x)=4-x^2$ from an earlier problem are shown together. Confirm from the picture that the region is symmetric about the $y$-axis, and use this to verify the earlier area answer $\frac{64}{3}$ using $2\int_0^2(8-2x^2)\,dx$.
questions.answer: The region is symmetric about $x=0$ since both curves are even functions. $2\int_0^2(8-2x^2)\,dx=2\left[8x-\frac{2x^3}{3}\right]_0^2=2\left(16-\frac{16}{3}\right)=2\cdot\frac{32}{3}=\frac{64}{3}$, matching the earlier full-interval computation.
